The thing is, a news source can be biased even if they only report facts. The key is that they can still avoid reporting things that go against their bias and focus on news that confirm it.

When the i was launched in the UK it used to be pretty impartial because it was so concise if didn't really have room for its writers to go on political rants. Now it is just big enough to allow for it to be left-wing.

It's impossible to remove bias entirely --- even deciding what story to report on and who to interview involves bias. But there are still some great news sources. The Wall Street Journal has a right-lean in its editorials, but on business reporting it's top notch. The New York Times leans the other way in editorials but no one is doing better investigative journalism.

If you're just looking to read news stories without opinion, news services like the AP, Reuters and AFP do a very good job.
